glosses: Inclined to contemplate; introspective and thoughtful; meditative.

examples.text: Compared with the greatest poets, he may be said to be the poet of unpoetical natures, possessed of quiet and contemplative tastes. glosses: Pertaining to a religious contemplative, or a contemplative religious orders, especially the Roman Catholic varieties.

examples.text: Whether the nuns of yore, being of a submissive rather than a stiff-necked generation, habitually bent their contemplative heads to avoid collision with the beams in the low ceilings of the many chambers of their House [...] may be matters of interest to its haunting ghosts (if any), but constitute no item in Miss Twinkleton's half-yearly accounts.

glosses: Relating to, or having the power of, contemplation.
